auth.description: DocuSign OAuth2 access token sent as a bearer; already minted, supplied through the environment
auth.name: docusign.access_token
auth.subject: unstated

config.help: The host portion of this account's own API server, without the https:// prefix — read it from the base_uri field of the accounts[] entry in DocuSign's OAuth UserInfo response (https://account-d.docusign.com/oauth/userinfo in the developer sandbox, https://account.docusign.com/oauth/userinfo in production) for the account you are connecting. If that field reads https://demo.docusign.net, enter demo.docusign.net
config.label: DocuSign account API host
config.name: account_host

config.help: This account's id (a GUID), from the same accounts[] entry of DocuSign's OAuth UserInfo response that account_host came from
config.label: DocuSign account id
config.name: account_id

config.help: An OAuth2 access token for this account — minted by DocuSign's own login flow or an integration key's JWT/authorization-code grant, and pasted here already-minted. It is short-lived; a call that starts failing with 401 usually means this needs refreshing
config.label: Access token
config.name: access_token

description: DocuSign eSignature REST API: list and read envelopes and their recipients, create an envelope from a template, and void one

operations.description: List the account's own top-level folders — Draft, Sent Items, Inbox, and any custom ones. Takes no parameters and succeeds for any account with API access, which is what makes it the connection check for a settings page's Test Connection button

response_schema.description: DocuSign's own folder structure, not envelope data

folders.description: Each folder's id and name, standard (Draft, Sent Items, Inbox, ...) and custom

operations.description: List envelopes whose status changed on or after a given date. DocuSign requires a from_date (or an explicit envelope_ids/transaction_ids list, which this operation does not offer) on every call to this resource — omitting it is a 400 from the vendor, not a limitation of this connector

params.description: Only envelopes with a status change on or after this date, as YYYY-MM-DD. Required — DocuSign's own resource has no unfiltered form
params.name: from_date

envelopes.description: Each envelope's own status summary — no recipient or document detail; see docusign-envelope-recipients-get for who is on it

status.description: e.g. sent, delivered, completed, declined, voided, created

resultSetSize.description: A COUNT, RETURNED AS A STRING — DocuSign's own convention, not this connector's

operations.description: Get one envelope's own status and metadata. No recipient or document detail — see docusign-envelope-recipients-get for who is on it

params.description: The envelope's DocuSign id (a GUID), as returned by docusign-envelope-list or docusign-envelope-create-from-template
params.name: envelope_id

status.description: e.g. sent, delivered, completed, declined, voided, created

voidedReason.description: Present only once the envelope has been voided

operations.description: Get every recipient on an envelope and their signing status. Recipient name and email are personal data — see this operation's own response_schema before logging, displaying or forwarding it

response_schema.description: Every recipient list here carries personal data: name and email identify a real person DocuSign is asking to sign, view or receive a copy. No example value is given anywhere in this connector for either field

agents.description: Recipients who may view and forward the envelope without signing. Same personal-data shape as signers

carbonCopies.description: Recipients who receive a copy once the envelope completes. Same personal-data shape as signers

recipientCount.description: A COUNT, RETURNED AS A STRING — DocuSign's own convention

email.description: Personal data — the signer's own email address

name.description: Personal data — the signer's own name

routingOrder.description: A COUNT, RETURNED AS A STRING — DocuSign's own convention

status.description: e.g. created, sent, delivered, completed, declined, autoresponded

operations.description: Create an envelope from an existing template. When status is sent, DocuSign dispatches it immediately to every named recipient — a real, legally binding signature request to a real person. Use status created to save it as an editable draft that notifies nobody instead

params.description: The template's id (a GUID) to generate the envelope from
params.name: templateId

params.description: One entry per role the template defines, supplying the recipient DocuSign routes that role to. email, name and roleName are all required by DocuSign. No example is given here — a signer's name and email are personal data — and roleName must match a role the template itself declares
params.name: templateRoles

email.description: Personal data. DocuSign routes and addresses the envelope using this address — a wrong value sends a real, legally binding signature request to the wrong person

name.description: Personal data. The recipient's name as it will appear on the signed document

roleName.description: Must match one of the roles the template itself defines

params.description: sent dispatches the envelope to every named recipient immediately; created saves it as an editable draft and notifies nobody
params.name: status

envelopeId.description: The new envelope's id — what docusign-envelope-get, docusign-envelope-recipients-get and docusign-envelope-void address it by

status.description: Echoes the status just set: sent or created

operations.description: Void an envelope: cancel it permanently. Every recipient who has not yet finished signing is immediately locked out, and no further signing action is possible on this envelope id. Irreversible

params.description: The envelope's DocuSign id (a GUID) to void
params.name: envelope_id

params.description: Why this envelope is being voided. DocuSign shows this to any recipient who already opened the envelope, so avoid putting anything sensitive in it
params.name: voidedReason
